newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends weaker, hits new contract lows.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends weaker, hits new contract lows.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed weaker after plunging to fresh contract lows for the third time this week amid a late-session bout of technically-driven selling, traders said.
Prices hovered close to unchanged and held over the contract lows made Thursday for most of the session as the trade remained a steady scale-down buyer.
Failing to make substantial gains, the selling dried up late in the day, allowing the benchmark December contract to fall under its previous low of 73.40 cents to 73.25 cents.
The contract ended down 0.68 cent at 73.35 cents per lb, having ranged from 74.20 to 73.25 cents. The rest of the board finished 0.62 to 0.18 cent lower.
Further losses are anticipated on Monday based on the weak technical close, analysts said. Support in December was seen at 72.00 cents followed by 70.35 cents, the now-expired July contract low.
"This doesn't look particularly healthy," John Moss, a technical analyst with Allendale said. "We've got a strong dollar that won't help us any (overseas)."

One Texas-based trader said the market is in a seasonal lull that could persist until the USDA issues its August supply and demand report, the first of the season to use state-by-state field surveys to gauge production.

Technically, many analysts were surprised by today's losses as the speculators are now believed to be holding a 15 to 18 percent net short position. NYCE reported on Tuesday that the speculators held a 38.2 percent net long position as of July 3.
Next week's spec/hedge report could provide some support, however, if the speculators are shown to be holding a 20 percent net short position, analysts said.
Monday's weekly crop condition report could also inspire a consolidation, they added.
An estimated 10,000 lots changed hands on the day compared with Thursday's official 21,-83 lots.

In its July report, the USDA put the 1997/98 crop at 18.0 million 480-lb bales versus 18.5 million bales in June. Exports were seen at 7.1 million bales compared with 7.3 million bales. Ending stocks remained unchanged at 3.95 million bales.
